stemMarkdown: A man travels from A to B at 54 km/h and returns along the same road at 48 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the two speeds. Taking the one-way distance as $d$: time $= \dfrac{d}{54} + \dfrac{d}{48}$, so average speed $= \dfrac{2d}{d/54 + d/48} = \dfrac{2 \times 54 \times 48}{54 + 48} = 50.8235$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For equal distances the answer is the harmonic mean. The plain average $\dfrac{54 + 48}{2} = 51.0$ is the classic wrong answer, and it is always too high.
